What is the equation of the ellipse given above?
worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(4,5),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=3,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=4.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-4)^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{{4}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-4)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{16} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Equations of Ellipses Centered at a General Point
